newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Normandy Mining executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny has attacked Prime Minister John Howard's speech on Aboriginal reconciliation at the Australian Reconciliation Convention, saying it set back the reconciliation process between Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal Australians and describing it as "totally inappropriate". Page 1.

Speaking at a Canberra symposium on Australia-Japan relations beyond 2000, Mitsui and Co Ltd executive managing director Seiji Kawarabayashi, one of Japan's most prominent businessmen, read the riot act to the Australian Federal Government on a wide rang of topics, including Australia's global competitiveness, industrial relations policy and unresolved native title issues. Page 3.

In a move designed to give priority to policies and the political strategy that the Federal Government will take to the next election, Prime Minister John Howard announced yesterday he would be reshaping his office. The reshuffle will see Howard's chief political adviser, Grahame Morris, also assuming the position of chief of staff. Page 3.

In a decision confirming the Australian Industrial Relations Commission's reluctance to include pay rises negotiated under collective bargaining in industrial awards, it yesterday rejected a push by building unions to increase award travel allowances in the construction industry by approximately A$30 a week. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Facing a hostile audience at yesterday's Aboriginal Reconciliation Conference, Prime Minister John Howard expressed deep personal sorrow over the stolen generation of Aborigines, but added that Australians of this generation should not accept the blame fo past actions and policies over which they had no control. Page 1.

Following a decision by each of Australia's four major banks to cut only 0.35 of a percentage point from their standard home loan rates, despite an official half-percentage point cut by the Reserve Bank, Prime Minister John Howard declared yesterday the banks' failure to pass on all of the cut was "unacceptable", while Federal Treasurer Peter Costello urged borrowers to switch to non-bank lenders. Page 1.

Following calls from New South Police for greater use of video cameras in public areas, Australia's first legislation to control video surveillance and covert photography in public places will be considered by the State Government today when it is presented within a New South Wales Law Reform Commission issues paper. Page 3.

Prominent businessman John Iliffe, 60, who became embroiled in controversy last year when he stood down as chairman of the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games to make way for New South Wales Olympics Minister Mr Knight, died on Saturday after "difficult and intrusive surgery" for terminal cancer. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Addressing more than 2,000 delegates from all States and Territories and from overseas at yesterday's Australian Reconciliation Convention opening, Prime Minister John Howard apologised personally for the "hurt and trauma" felt by Aborigines who had been forcibly removed from their parents, and defended his Wik native title plan. Page 1.

A breakthrough in talks over the stalled A$1.2 billion Lake Cowal goldmine near West Wyalong in New South Wales, may see the project go ahead under a compromise plan being put forward by environmentalists that includes a demand that resources group North Ltd pay to turn the lake area into a nature reserve. Page 1.

Five hundred people were evacuated from Sydney's Skygarden Shopping Centre yesterday and part of the street cordoned off after 29 workers from a city solicitor's office and a fireman were overcome by fumes from a pesticide spill and taken to hospital. Pag 3.

According to local Sydney doctors, individual waiting lists kept by surgeons, and the official average waiting times sent out to local GPs by the Central Sydney Area Health Service for some central and south-east Sydney hospitals can vary by nine months or more, making them virtually meaningless. Page 3.
THE AGE

Part of the 1,800-strong audience at yesterday's first national convention on reconciliation yelled abuse and turned their backs on Prime Minister John Howard when he angrily defended his controversial 10-point native title plan. Howard also received a mixed response to his rejection of the idea that today's generation of Australians should accept blame or guilt for the forced separation of Aboriginal children from their parents. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello told Parliament yesterday the four big banks' decision on Friday to reduce interest rates by 0.35 per cent instead of the 0.5 per cent cut in official rates meant that the Wallis inquiry recommendations to subject banks to more competition were now appealing, warning the banks to deliver the rates cut in full. Page 1.

According to David Marshall, Queensland University's English and cultural studies department head, and author of a new book, Celebrity and Power: Fame in Contemporary Culture, television celebrity Sam Newman, who was recently run over by his own car behind his home, typifies Australians' love of accessible heroes. Page 1.

The Australian Football League Tribunal last night suspended West Coast's Chris Lewis, who pleaded guilty to two striking charges against Essendon players Barry Young and Danny Morgan in Sunday night's game. Lewis told the Tribunal he was disappointed in is actions, and West Coast football manager Trevor Nisbett said Lewis had been counselled to rectify his misplaced aggression in the past. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
